summary:
# NOTES ON THE THREE BOOKS (for later question answering)

## BOOK 1 — "The Runaways" by Nat Gould (Gutenberg #39631)

**Front matter:** Appreciation by E. Laton Blacklands; Nat Gould b. Manchester 1857, d. 1919; journalist in England and Australia; hobbies racing, driving, gardening. Publisher G. Heath Robinson & J. Birch Ltd.

**Characters:** Redmond Maynard (the Squire, Hazelwell); Ulick Maynard (his son, left home two years earlier after accusation); Irene Carstone/Courtly (ward of Squire, daughter of Colonel Carstone; married Warren Courtly); Warren Courtly (of Anselm Manor, gambler); Bersak (Squire's wolf-hound; once saved Ulick from a bull); Eli Todd (stud manager, ex-Hussars with Colonel Carstone); Janet Todd (Eli's daughter, vain, ran off); Bob Heather (groom/driver); Mary Marley (Irene's maid, later Bob's wife); Mrs. Marley (housekeeper at Hazelwell); Martha Dixon (housekeeper at Anselm Manor); James Bard (vet, Helton); Sam Lane (huntsman); Fred May (trainer, Stanton House, Newmarket); Ben Sprig (jockey, "saints be praised"); Conrad Rush (owner of Kit Cat); Felix Hoffman (racecourse sharper, Feltham, blackmailer); Mrs. Hoffman; Dr. Harding; Lady Ada—no, Ada not in Book 1; Joe (Eli's stud hand); Josh (publican); Dyer (rider); Milander (hurdler); Sandstone (Derby winner); Vulture (American-owned); Coralie; Avenger; Decoy Duck; Mermaid; Pinkerton; Mulgar; Ringbell.

**Horses:** Random (bay hunter Ulick's favourite, given to Irene; Irene painted him); Rupert (Irene's mount, dark brown); Honeysuckle (old mare, won Oaks and St Leger; foaled colt New Year's Eve, quarter hour after midnight); the Saint (grey two-year-old, Father Confessor out of Hilda, bought by Ulick for 200 guineas via Fred May, race name Mr. Lanark, olive green colours; won Pastures Handicap at Kempton, Coronation Cup at Epsom by a short head over Vulture); "Tone river"; Blossom; Scout (Viceroy's Cup second); Soup Ladle.

**Plot:** Night of anniversary (New Year's Eve/night two years on); Squire sits up. Ulick, accused of seducing Janet, left after bitter words ("Good-night"). Irene stays at Hazelwell on snow night; Redmond feels Warren's neglect. Irene paints Random, takes it to Hazelwell; sends £5 to Felix Hoffman (Feltham, Middlesex, 25 Main Street); Warren's scented letter. Honeysuckle foals; Ulick visits Eli secretly; reveals address; Eli says Janet is the girl who ran away the same night. Warren had tricked Janet, installed her as "Mrs. Warren" at Hoffman's, Feltham. Warren sells Holme Farm for £10,000 to pay gambling debts. Felix blackmails Warren (£50); Irene gets Felix's second letter, goes to Feltham, meets Janet; Janet confesses. Squire and Ulick reconcile at Newmarket (Fred May, Eli arrange), Walton Hotel. Derby day Sandstone wins; Coronation Cup Saint wins; Warren confesses to Irene; Irene refuses to tell Squire until... Warren leaves to ride; jumps churchyard wall at Glen church chasing Ulick (rode Random), dies (neck broken) on Harewood's vault. Janet returns to Eli; Eli: "Warrren Courtly" induced it. Epilogue: Ulick marries Irene; child; Janet becomes Irene's maid; Felix flees; Saint at Hazelwell stud.

## BOOK 2 — "Just a Girl" by Charles Garvice (Gutenberg #57166)

**Setting:** Three Star Camp, Australian gold camp; Dan MacGrath's Eldorado saloon; Dog's Ear rival camp; Wally River/Valley; Ballarat, Melbourne, Good Luck, Wally-Wally, Green Bank, Gulch.

**Characters:** Varley Howard (professional gambler, tall silk hat, diamond scarf-pin, won the baby by cards); Esmeralda Howard (foundling, auburn-gold hair, dark brown eyes, freckles); Bill the postman (finds baby on dead woman, three-mile road to Dog's Ear); Mother Melinda; Taffy (Welsh giant); The Penman (schoolmaster); Dan MacGrath; the doctor ("the Parson"); Simon (Dog's Ear villain); Lord Norman Druce (Oakfield, Manor; "Pink Rosebud"); Mr. Samson Pinchook (solicitor, Pinchook, Pinchook & Becham, 119 Grey's Inn); Gordon Chetwynde (millionaire grandfather, £2 millions); Lady Wyndover (guardian, Grosvenor Square, Mount Street dressmaker Madame Cerise); Barker (maid); Lord Trafford (Marquis, eldest son of Duke of Belfayre; Albany chambers); Duke of Belfayre (father, kind, dying); Lilias Selvaine (cousin, small, dark, grey eyes); Lord Selvaine (uncle, bachelor, cynical); Lady Ada Lancing (Scots peer's daughter, Lady Grange guardian, Eaton Square); Mr. Helby (steward); Lord Blankyre and Lady Blankyre; Lady Lilias; Lord Chesterleigh; Lady Mary; Lord Villiers; Lord Ffoulkes (best man); Mr. Elmbourne (PM); Felix? no.

**Key events in order:** Baby found in road → won at cards by Varley (six men, highest cards); named Esmeralda Howard; camp adores her. Taught by The Penman; love talk with Varley. Norman Druce wounded, rescued by Esmeralda from Dog's Ear ambush (her hat bullet-holed). Norman sings at Eldorado; declares love by river; she refuses. Pinchook arrives; Varley sends her to England. Lady Wyndover; Cerise dresses; Blankyre party; Lord Selvaine; Trafford meets Esmeralda in park (she rescued Lady Ada's horse). Trafford's uncle proposes marriage plan. Trafford visits Lady Ada, says goodbye. Belfayre; watering-place scheme. Trafford proposes on Shirley drive (Esmeralda drives). Wedding at church; Ada bridesmaid. Wedding night: Esmeralda learns he married for money; "No!" Trafford's note: she removes ring; leaves Belfayre; duke dies in sleep. Ada gives Trafford Norman's letter; Trafford thinks Norman and Esmeralda lovers; Norman rushed to mother, then follows to Australia. Esmeralda returns to Three Star; is kidnapped by Simon; escapes with revolver; Trafford and Varley duel; Esmeralda throws herself between; Varley's bullet hits her shoulder. Trafford forgives; reunited at hut; wedding-like reunion. Epilogue: Lord Selvaine's cable; Norman marries Lilias; Varley visits England; Lady Ada left for Continent.

## BOOK 3 — "Tinman" by Tom Gallon (Gutenberg #48989)

**Narrator:** Charles Avaline, the Tinman (prison No. 145). Born ~1880 (age 20 at crime; in prison 20 years; now ~40).

**Part I:** Guardian Jervis Fanshawe (office in City, Patton & Co.; thin, long face, wide nostrils, cut in chin; fingers twining). Gavin Hockley (big swaggering young man, moustache, cane; gambler, blackmailer, loud). Hammerstone Market (country town, the George hotel; Patton's house). Barbara Patton (18, fair, sunlit; sang; mother's voice). Lucas Savell (good-humoured cousin, fiancé). Mr. Patton (old, kindly, dictatorial). Dawkins; Murray Olivant (Murray Olivant, rich, cane). Charles's I.O.U. debts; card game; Hockley taunts "Lucky at cards, unlucky in love." Charles strikes Hockley on terrace; overturns; later fight in inn; threats "I'll make you eat your lie." Charles goes to Hockley's rooms in Lincoln's Inn Fields and kills him with a sword (two blows). Fanshawe had engineered it (manipulated). Charles confesses to Fanshawe; sentenced to death; commuted to penal servitude for life on account of youth. Barbara's note: "My dear Prince Charlie…". Barbara visits prison in dream and in person before the hanging; forbids telling truth.

**Part II:** Release after 20 years (No. 145). Fanshawe waits at gates (Jervis Fanshawe, "Moggs" the girl at Thames-side lodging). Murray Olivant (wealthy; Bloomsbury?/ fashionable flat; manservant) takes Charles as "Tinman." Hammerstone Market: Barbara Savell (daughter of Barbara Avaline née Patton and Lucas Savell; the elder Barbara is alive, under name Barbara Avaline); young Arnold Millard (half-brother of Olivant; painter; Barbara's lover). Dawkins (smiling). Olivant seizes Barbara; Arnold fights him; Olivant tricks Tinman into imprisonment with forged note; Dawkins takes Barbara to London. Moggs rescues Barbara. Fanshawe steals tickets for voyage on the *Eaglet*; Olivant apparently sails. Fanshawe kills Olivant in Lincoln's Inn Fields rooms with sailor's knife (Olivant's rooms, Tinman's keys). Fanshawe dies aboard *Eaglet* (wrecked off Ushant, Henry Howard only survivor). Elder Barbara finds Lucas Savell, who has a stroke (silent). Barbara Savell marries Arnold Millard. Ending: Charles (Tinman) takes name Avaline again with Barbara (elder), who "takes his name."

**Notes:** Numbers: prison No. 145; £5 cheque; I.O.U. ~£30 then ~£70; £10,000 no; prison 20 years. Places: Hammerstone Market, Lincoln's Inn Fields, Holborn, Bloomsbury, the George, Feltham-like docks, Ushant.
